$$\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Bigl\lvert q\,D_a(b+Qt) - \operatorname{round}\bigl(q\,D_a(b+Qt)\bigr)\Bigr\rvert \le q\sum_{p\mid a}\Bigl(\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{T}\Bigr),\qquad D_a(m) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\omega\bigl(a(m+k+1)\bigr)}{2^{k+1}}$$

For naturals q and an integer z with q·∑_{n≥0} ω(n)/2^n = z, and for naturals a, Q, b, T with a ≠ 0, T > 0 and every prime factor p of a coprime to Q, the average over t < T of the distance from q·D_a(b+Qt) to its nearest integer is at most q times the sum over the prime factors p of a of 1/p + 1/T. Everything is in ℝ: ω(n) is the number of distinct prime factors of n, `round` is Mathlib's rounding (half rounds up), the sum over p ∣ a runs over `a.primeFactors`, and each series is a tsum (0 when not summable).
label: A rational series puts dilated tails near integers
